items.shortDefinition: Root anatomical hierarchy encompassing central and peripheral divisions of the human nervous system.
items.biologicalRole: Integrates sensory transduction, internal computation, homeostatic regulation, and motor execution across the organism.

items.shortDefinition: Encephalon (brain) and spinal cord enclosed within the cranial vault, vertebral canal, and meninges.
items.biologicalRole: Primary integrative and computational core of the nervous system.

items.shortDefinition: Cranial nerves, spinal nerves, dorsal root ganglia, and autonomic ganglia outside the pial-glial limitans.
items.biologicalRole: Conveys afferent sensory signals to CNS and efferent somatic/autonomic commands to effector organs.

items.shortDefinition: Intracranial division of the CNS comprising forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain.
items.biologicalRole: Mediates perception, motor control, homeostatic regulation, emotion, language, and cognition.

items.shortDefinition: Rostral brain vesicle comprising telencephalon (cerebral hemispheres, basal ganglia, limbic structures) and diencephalon.
items.biologicalRole: Supports higher-order sensory, motor, associative, limbic, and neuroendocrine integration.

items.shortDefinition: Cerebral cortex, subcortical white matter, basal ganglia, hippocampal formation, and amygdala.
items.biologicalRole: Largest division of the human brain mediating cortical and subcortical computation.

items.shortDefinition: Midline forebrain complex surrounding the third ventricle, including thalamus, hypothalamus, epithalamus, and subthalamus.
items.biologicalRole: Central relay for sensory/motor/limbic loops and master regulator of autonomic and circadian homeostasis.

items.shortDefinition: Left half of the cerebrum separated from the right hemisphere by the longitudinal cerebral fissure.
items.biologicalRole: Processes contralateral right-sided sensorimotor space and typically dominates language production/comprehension.

items.shortDefinition: Right half of the cerebrum linked to the left hemisphere via commissural tracts.
items.biologicalRole: Processes contralateral left-sided sensorimotor space and contributes strongly to visuospatial orienting and prosody.

items.shortDefinition: Largest commissural white-matter bundle (~200 million axons) comprising rostrum, genu, body, and splenium.
items.biologicalRole: Synchronizes and transfers sensorimotor and associative information between homotopic and heterotopic cortical areas.

items.shortDefinition: Compact commissural fiber bundle crossing rostral to the columns of the fornix.
items.biologicalRole: Interconnects bilateral temporal lobes, olfactory bulbs, and amygdaloid complexes.

items.shortDefinition: Dorsal epithalamic/pretectal commissure at the junction of third ventricle and cerebral aqueduct.
items.biologicalRole: Mediates consensual pupillary light reflex by coupling bilateral pretectal and Edinger-Westphal nuclei.

items.shortDefinition: Anterior cerebral lobe rostral to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus.
items.biologicalRole: Houses primary motor, premotor, supplementary motor, Broca's speech, and prefrontal executive/valuation cortices.

items.shortDefinition: Dorsoposterior cerebral lobe bounded by the central sulcus rostrally and parieto-occipital sulcus caudally.
items.biologicalRole: Processes somatosensory touch/proprioception, multisensory spatial coordinate transformations, and dorsal attention.

items.shortDefinition: Ventrolateral cerebral lobe inferior to the lateral (Sylvian) fissure.
items.biologicalRole: Contains primary/association auditory cortex, ventral visual object stream, lexical-semantic networks, and medial temporal memory structures.

items.shortDefinition: Posterior cerebral lobe surrounding the calcarine sulcus.
items.biologicalRole: Dedicated to early and intermediate retinotopic visual processing (V1, V2, V3, V4).

items.shortDefinition: Deep cerebral cortex buried within the floor of the lateral sulcus and covered by frontal/parietal/temporal opercula.
items.biologicalRole: Integrates viscerosensory interoception, gustation, nociceptive salience, and autonomic regulation.

items.shortDefinition: Medial cortical ring comprising cingulate, parahippocampal, and subcallosal gyri encircling the corpus callosum and diencephalon.
items.biologicalRole: Coordinates emotion, episodic memory routing, autonomic state, and default-mode internal cognition.

items.shortDefinition: Frontal gyrus immediately anterior to the central sulcus corresponding to Brodmann Area 4.
items.biologicalRole: Somatotopically organized origin of corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts controlling voluntary movement.

items.shortDefinition: Parietal gyrus immediately posterior to the central sulcus encompassing Brodmann Areas 3a, 3b, 1, and 2.
items.biologicalRole: Receives VPL/VPM thalamic relays for discriminative touch, vibration, and proprioception.

items.shortDefinition: Dorsal frontal gyrus extending onto the medial surface including the supplementary motor area (SMA).
items.biologicalRole: Supports motor sequence planning, working memory maintenance, and cognitive control.

items.shortDefinition: Middle frontal gyral association cortex (BA 9/46) with dense recurrent Layer 3 pyramidal networks.
items.biologicalRole: Core hub of the frontoparietal network mediating working memory manipulation, rule maintenance, and executive control.

items.shortDefinition: Ventrolateral frontal gyrus comprising pars opercularis (BA 44), pars triangularis (BA 45), and pars orbitalis (BA 47).
items.biologicalRole: Participates in phonological-articulatory dorsal-stream speech sequencing, syntactic unification, and inhibitory control.

items.shortDefinition: Ventral prefrontal cortex overlying the orbital plates and medial frontal wall (BA 10/11/14/25/32).
items.biologicalRole: Encodes subjective outcome value, reward expectation, autonomic regulation, and fear extinction gating.

items.canonicalName: Superior Temporal Gyrus & Primary Auditory Cortex (A1)
aliases: Superior Temporal Gyrus & Primary Auditory Cortex
items.shortDefinition: Dorsal temporal gyrus housing Heschl's transverse gyri (A1, BA 41/42) and Wernicke-related posterior STG (BA 22).
items.biologicalRole: Performs tonotopic auditory analysis, spectrotemporal speech decoding, and auditory-motor integration.

items.shortDefinition: Ventral occipitotemporal gyrus bounded medially by the collateral sulcus.
items.biologicalRole: High-level ventral visual stream hub mediating invariant object, face, and word-form recognition.

items.shortDefinition: Multimodal temporoparietal association cortex (BA 39 and BA 40).
items.biologicalRole: Integrates phonological, semantic, attentional reorienting, and praxis representations.

items.shortDefinition: Medial arch of cortex superior to the corpus callosum, divided into anterior (ACC) and posterior (PCC) zones.
items.biologicalRole: Links conflict/salience monitoring and pain affect (ACC) with default-mode autobiographical integration (PCC).

items.shortDefinition: Rostral and dorsal cingulate zone (BA 24/32/25) connected to insula, amygdala, and prefrontal cortex.
items.biologicalRole: Mediates cognitive conflict monitoring, effort valuation, autonomic arousal, and affective pain processing.

items.shortDefinition: Caudal medial parietal/cingulate hub (BA 23/31) exhibiting high baseline metabolic rate.
items.biologicalRole: Core structural and functional connector hub of the Default Mode Network and episodic retrieval circuit.

items.shortDefinition: Medial temporal gyrus encompassing entorhinal, perirhinal, and parahippocampal cortices.
items.biologicalRole: Primary cortical interface funneling multimodal neocortical associations into and out of the hippocampal formation.

items.shortDefinition: Deep landmark sulcus separating the frontal lobe (M1) from the parietal lobe (S1).
items.biologicalRole: Anatomical boundary dividing primary motor output cortex from primary somatosensory input cortex.

items.shortDefinition: Deep cleft separating frontal and parietal lobes superiorly from the temporal lobe inferiorly, housing the insula.
items.biologicalRole: Major perisylvian anatomical landmark enclosing auditory, insular, and language networks.

items.shortDefinition: Medial occipital sulcus flanked by striate cortex (Brodmann Area 17 / V1, Gennari's stripe in Layer 4B).
items.biologicalRole: Receives retinotopic optic radiation inputs from LGN and extracts local orientation, spatial frequency, and ocular dominance.

items.shortDefinition: Superficial cortical laminae containing apical tufts (L1) and dense cortico-cortical pyramidal neurons (L2/3).
items.biologicalRole: Principal source and target of horizontal, associative, and feedforward/feedback intracortical connections.

items.shortDefinition: Thalamorecipient granular Layer IV, subcortically projecting Layer V pyramidal cells, and corticothalamic Layer VI.
items.biologicalRole: Receives core thalamic relays (L4) and dispatches motor/striatal/brainstem (L5) and thalamic feedback (L6) outputs.

items.shortDefinition: Medial temporal allocortical complex comprising dentate gyrus, hippocampus proper (CA3/CA2/CA1), subiculum, and entorhinal interface.
items.biologicalRole: Essential biological substrate for episodic memory encoding, spatial cognitive mapping, and sharp-wave ripple consolidation.

items.shortDefinition: Three-layered archicortical structure subdivided into CA3, CA2, and CA1 fields along the hippocampal transverse axis.
items.biologicalRole: Executes auto-associative pattern completion (CA3) and sequence comparison/output routing (CA1).

items.shortDefinition: Dense granule-cell layer receiving perforant path axons from entorhinal cortex and projecting unmyelinated mossy fibers to CA3.
items.biologicalRole: Performs sparse-coding expansion recoding and orthogonalization (pattern separation) of overlapping cortical inputs.

items.shortDefinition: Proximal Cornu Ammonis subfield receiving dentate mossy fibers and elaborating extensive recurrent collateral axons.
items.biologicalRole: Acts as an auto-associative attractor network capable of cue-triggered pattern completion and sharp-wave generation.

items.shortDefinition: Compact Cornu Ammonis zone intercalated between CA3 and CA1 with distinct vasopressin/oxytocin receptor expression.
items.biologicalRole: Modulates social memory recognition and gates propagation between CA3 and CA1.

items.shortDefinition: Distal Cornu Ammonis subfield receiving CA3 Schaffer collaterals in stratum radiatum and direct EC L3 inputs in stratum lacunosum-moleculare.
items.biologicalRole: Compares stored CA3 predictions with current entorhinal sensory reality and serves as the classic locus of NMDA-dependent LTP.

items.shortDefinition: Transition zone between three-layered CA1 and six-layered presubiculum/entorhinal cortex.
items.biologicalRole: Major output stage of the hippocampus projecting via the fornix and back to deep entorhinal layers.

items.shortDefinition: Anterior parahippocampal allocortex (BA 28) containing grid cells in medial EC and object-context cells in lateral EC.
items.biologicalRole: Bidirectional gateway between neocortex and hippocampus via the perforant and temporoammonic pathways.

items.shortDefinition: Almond-shaped nuclear complex in the anteromedial temporal lobe comprising basolateral, central, and corticomedial groups.
items.biologicalRole: Evaluates emotional valence and threat/reward salience, coordinating defensive, autonomic, and memory modulation.

items.shortDefinition: Cortex-like glutamatergic + GABAergic interneuron complex (lateral, basal, and accessory basal nuclei).
items.biologicalRole: Primary sensory input stage of the amygdala where conditioned-unconditioned stimulus associations undergo LTP.

items.shortDefinition: Striatum-like GABAergic output nucleus of the amygdala projecting to hypothalamus, PAG, and brainstem autonomic centers.
items.biologicalRole: Drives physiological, autonomic, and behavioral expression of defensive and stress responses.

items.shortDefinition: Subcallosal basal forebrain cholinergic and GABAergic pacemaker nuclei connected to hippocampus via the fornix.
items.biologicalRole: Paces hippocampal theta oscillations (4-8 Hz) essential for active spatial and episodic encoding.

items.shortDefinition: Interconnected subcortical nuclei comprising striatum, pallidum, subthalamic nucleus, and substantia nigra.
items.biologicalRole: Gates action selection, motor vigor, habit learning, and reinforcement-driven value updating via parallel thalamocortical loops.

items.shortDefinition: Primary input stage of the basal ganglia encompassing caudate nucleus, putamen, and ventral striatum (nucleus accumbens).
items.biologicalRole: Integrates glutamatergic cortical/thalamic inputs with midbrain dopaminergic RPE signals onto D1 and D2 medium spiny neurons.

items.shortDefinition: C-shaped dorsal striatal nucleus (head, body, tail) bordering the lateral ventricle.
items.biologicalRole: Receives prefrontal and parietal association inputs supporting goal-directed cognitive and oculomotor control.

items.shortDefinition: Lateral dorsal striatal nucleus lateral to the globus pallidus and medial to the external capsule.
items.biologicalRole: Receives somatotopic sensorimotor cortical projections mediating motor execution and procedural habit learning.

items.shortDefinition: Ventromedial striatal core and shell receiving dense VTA dopamine, amygdala, hippocampal subiculum, and vmPFC inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Central limbic-motor interface translating reward prediction errors and motivational salience into action vigor.

items.shortDefinition: Tonically active GABAergic pallidal nucleus inhibited by D2 indirect-pathway striatal medium spiny neurons.
items.biologicalRole: Inhibits the subthalamic nucleus and coordinates indirect-pathway motor suppression.

items.shortDefinition: Principal GABAergic output nucleus of the basal ganglia (functionally homologous with SNr).
items.biologicalRole: Tonically inhibits VL/VA motor thalamus; transient pauses induced by D1 direct-pathway input disinhibit movement.

items.shortDefinition: Lens-shaped glutamatergic diencephalic nucleus receiving hyperdirect frontal cortical input and GPe inhibition.
items.biologicalRole: Provides fast global excitatory drive to GPi/SNr to brake or cancel premature motor actions.

items.shortDefinition: Midbrain nuclear complex divided into dopaminergic pars compacta (SNc, nigrostriatal pathway) and GABAergic pars reticulata (SNr).
items.biologicalRole: SNc modulates dorsal striatal D1/D2 excitability via dopamine; SNr gates superior colliculus and thalamic oculomotor outputs.

items.shortDefinition: Paired egg-shaped diencephalic nuclear complex subdivided by the internal medullary lamina into anterior, medial, and lateral nuclear groups.
items.biologicalRole: Gates and transforms sensory, motor, and associative cortico-thalamo-cortical information across wakefulness and sleep.

items.shortDefinition: Somatosensory relay nucleus receiving the medial lemniscus (DCML) and spinothalamic tracts from the body and limbs.
items.biologicalRole: Relays somatotopic mechanosensory and nociceptive signals from the trunk and extremities to S1.

items.shortDefinition: Somatosensory and gustatory relay nucleus receiving trigeminothalamic (CN V) and solitary tract (rNTS) inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Relays facial somatosensation to lateral S1 and gustatory signals (via VPMpc) to anterior insula.

items.canonicalName: Ventral Lateral & Ventral Anterior Thalamic Nuclei (VL / VA)
aliases: Ventral Lateral & Ventral Anterior Thalamic Nuclei
items.shortDefinition: Motor thalamic relay nuclei receiving pallidal (GPi/SNr) inhibition and deep cerebellar (dentate) excitation.
items.biologicalRole: Transmits basal ganglia and cerebellar motor loop signals to primary motor (M1) and premotor cortices.

items.shortDefinition: Six-layered visual thalamic nucleus (magnocellular layers 1-2, parvocellular layers 3-6, koniocellular interlaminar).
items.biologicalRole: Relays contralateral visual hemifield retinal ganglion cell inputs via the optic radiations to V1 Layer 4C.

items.shortDefinition: Auditory thalamic nucleus (ventral tonotopic, dorsal, and medial divisions) receiving inferior colliculus inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Relays frequency-organized auditory signals to primary auditory cortex (A1) in Heschl's gyrus.

items.shortDefinition: Large association nucleus medial to the internal medullary lamina reciprocally connected with prefrontal cortex and amygdala.
items.biologicalRole: Sustains persistent prefrontal working-memory activity and executive rule switching.

items.shortDefinition: Largest posterior association nucleus of the human thalamus interconnected with occipital, parietal, and temporal cortices.
items.biologicalRole: Synchronizes cortico-cortical alpha/gamma communication to gate visual attention and salience.

items.shortDefinition: Thin shell of parvalbumin-rich GABAergic neurons enveloping the lateral thalamus, innervated by thalamocortical and corticothalamic collaterals.
items.biologicalRole: Paces sleep spindles, alpha oscillations, and selective attentional gating by inhibiting thalamocortical relay nuclei.

items.shortDefinition: Ventral diencephalic nuclear complex forming the floor and lower walls of the third ventricle above the pituitary gland.
items.biologicalRole: Integrates thermoregulation, circadian rhythms, sleep-wake switching, hunger/satiety, autonomic output, and neuroendocrine HPA/HPG axes.

items.shortDefinition: Paired anterior hypothalamic nucleus immediately dorsal to the optic chiasm receiving retinohypothalamic ipRGC inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Master mammalian circadian pacemaker (~20,000 neurons) synchronizing 24-hour physiological rhythms via CLOCK:BMAL1/PER:CRY loops.

items.shortDefinition: Medial hypothalamic nucleus containing magnocellular (oxytocin/vasopressin) and parvocellular (CRH/TRH + pre-autonomic) neurons.
items.biologicalRole: Drives the HPA stress axis (CRH -> ACTH -> cortisol) and descending sympathetic/parasympathetic brainstem control.

items.shortDefinition: Neuroendocrine gland suspended in the sella turcica comprising adenohypophysis (anterior) and neurohypophysis (posterior).
items.biologicalRole: Secretes systemic peptide hormones in response to hypothalamic releasing factors and posterior magnocellular axon terminals.

items.shortDefinition: Posterior fossa hindbrain structure containing >50% of all human brain neurons, divided into vermis, paravermis, hemispheres, and flocculonodular lobe.
items.biologicalRole: Computes real-time sensorimotor forward models, motor timing, vestibulo-ocular calibration, and cognitive sequence prediction.

items.shortDefinition: Highly regular three-layered foliar cortex where granule parallel fibers and inferior olivary climbing fibers converge on Purkinje cells.
items.biologicalRole: Executes high-dimensional expansion recoding and supervised error-driven LTD/LTP at parallel-fiber to Purkinje synapses.

items.shortDefinition: Midline spinocerebellar zone receiving proprioceptive, vestibular, and visual posture inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Regulates axial musculature, gait posture, and saccadic accuracy via the fastigial nucleus.

items.shortDefinition: Phylogenetically oldest cerebellar lobe reciprocally connected with the brainstem vestibular nuclei.
items.biologicalRole: Calibrates the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), smooth pursuit eye movements, and balance.

items.shortDefinition: Deep output nuclei embedded in cerebellar white matter receiving inhibitory Purkinje axons and excitatory mossy/climbing collaterals.
items.biologicalRole: Sole output stage of the cerebellum projecting via the superior cerebellar peduncle to VL thalamus and red nucleus.

items.shortDefinition: Three paired white-matter stalks linking cerebellum to midbrain (SCP efferent), pons (MCP corticopontocerebellar afferent), and medulla (ICP).
items.biologicalRole: Convey massive cortico-ponto-cerebellar input, spinocerebellar/olivary feedback, and dentato-rubro-thalamic output.

items.shortDefinition: Posterior brain division comprising pons, medulla oblongata, and cerebellum surrounding the fourth ventricle.
items.biologicalRole: Integrates cranial nerve nuclei, cardiorespiratory vitality centers, ascending/descending tracts, and cerebellar loops.

items.shortDefinition: Rostral brainstem segment comprising tectum (colliculi), tegmentum (VTA, red nucleus, PAG), and cerebral peduncles.
items.biologicalRole: Coordinates orienting reflexes, dopaminergic reward/motor signaling, descending analgesia, and oculomotor control.

items.shortDefinition: Layered dorsal midbrain tectal nucleus receiving direct retinal, visual cortical, auditory, and SNr inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Generates rapid saccadic eye movements and multisensory spatial orienting toward salient stimuli.

items.shortDefinition: Caudal midbrain tectal nucleus receiving ascending lateral lemniscus binaural auditory pathways.
items.biologicalRole: Obligatory midbrain convergence hub for auditory frequency, timing, and localization prior to MGN relay.

items.shortDefinition: Medial midbrain tegmental cluster of dopaminergic (A10), GABAergic, and glutamatergic neurons.
items.biologicalRole: Origin of mesolimbic and mesocortical dopamine pathways broadcasting reward prediction errors to NAc and PFC.

items.shortDefinition: Columnar gray matter surrounding the cerebral aqueduct innervated by hypothalamus, CeA, ACC, and spinomesencephalic tracts.
items.biologicalRole: Coordinates descending opioid/serotonergic/noradrenergic pain suppression (via RVM) and defensive freezing/flight behaviors.

items.shortDefinition: Middle brainstem division between midbrain and medulla containing basis pontis nuclei and pontine tegmentum.
items.biologicalRole: Relays massive corticopontocerebellar traffic and houses CN V–VIII nuclei, locus coeruleus, and pontine respiratory/REM centers.

items.shortDefinition: Dorsolateral pontine tegmental nucleus (A6) providing the primary noradrenergic innervation to forebrain, cerebellum, and spinal cord.
items.biologicalRole: Modulates global neural gain, pupil-linked arousal, attentional alerting, and exploration-exploitation trade-offs.

items.shortDefinition: Midline brainstem serotonergic cell groups (B1–B9) spanning midbrain, pons, and medulla.
items.biologicalRole: Diffuse serotonergic projections regulating sleep-wake cycles, affective tone, patience, and dorsal-horn pain gating.

items.shortDefinition: Caudal brainstem segment continuous with the spinal cord at the foramen magnum, housing pyramids, olives, and CN IX–XII.
items.biologicalRole: Contains vital cardiovascular, baroreflex, and respiratory rhythm-generating centers (pre-Bötzinger complex).

items.shortDefinition: Dorsomedial medullary sensory nucleus receiving visceral and gustatory afferents from CN VII, IX, and X.
items.biologicalRole: Rostral NTS relays taste to VPMpc; caudal NTS integrates baroreceptor, chemoreceptor, and gastrointestinal vagal reflexes.

items.canonicalName: Vestibular Nuclear Complex (Superior, Lateral, Medial, Inferior)
items.shortDefinition: Floor of fourth ventricle nuclear complex at the pontomedullary junction receiving CN VIII vestibular afferents.
items.biologicalRole: Drives vestibulo-ocular (MLF) and vestibulospinal reflexes maintaining gaze stability and antigravity posture.

items.shortDefinition: Interconnected ependymal-lined cavities producing, circulating, and cushioning the CNS with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
items.biologicalRole: Produces ~500 mL/day of CSF via choroid plexus, providing mechanical buoyancy, ionic homeostasis, and glymphatic clearance.

items.shortDefinition: Paired C-shaped cerebral cavities (anterior horn, body, atrium, inferior/temporal horn, posterior/occipital horn) draining via foramina of Monro.
items.biologicalRole: Border the caudate nucleus, corpus callosum, thalamus, and hippocampus; adult SVZ neurogenic niche lines the lateral wall.

items.shortDefinition: Narrow midline diencephalic cleft between the thalami and hypothalami draining caudally through the aqueduct of Sylvius.
items.biologicalRole: Bathes hypothalamic circumventricular organs and conducts CSF from lateral ventricles to the fourth ventricle.

items.shortDefinition: Diamond-shaped hindbrain cavity between pons/medulla anteriorly and cerebellum posteriorly, exiting via foramina of Luschka and Magendie.
items.biologicalRole: Conveys CSF into the subarachnoid cisterns and overlies vital brainstem nuclei in the rhomboid fossa.

items.canonicalName: Cranial Meninges (Dura, Arachnoid, Pia) & Blood-Brain Barrier
items.shortDefinition: Three protective connective-tissue membranes, dural venous sinuses, subarachnoid space, and neurovascular endothelial tight junctions.
items.biologicalRole: Protects the CNS mechanically, drains CSF and meningeal lymphatics, and restricts paracellular solute entry via the BBB.

items.shortDefinition: Segmental cylindrical CNS structure extending from the foramen magnum to the conus medullaris (L1/L2 vertebral level).
items.biologicalRole: Conveys ascending sensory and descending motor tracts and executes segmental spinal reflexes and central pattern generation.

items.canonicalName: Spinal Cord Dorsal Horn (Rexed Laminae I–VI)
items.shortDefinition: Posterior spinal gray matter column including marginal zone (Lamina I), substantia gelatinosa (Lamina II), and nucleus proprius.
items.biologicalRole: First synaptic processing and gating stage for nociceptive, thermal, and mechanosensory dorsal root ganglion afferents.

items.canonicalName: Spinal Cord Ventral & Lateral Horns (Rexed Laminae VII–IX)
items.tnaLatinName: Cornu anterius et laterale medullae spinalis
aliases: Cornu anterius et laterale medullae spinalis
items.shortDefinition: Anterior spinal gray matter housing alpha/gamma motor neuron pools and Renshaw/Ia interneurons, plus T1–L2/S2–S4 autonomic columns.
items.biologicalRole: Final common pathway driving skeletal muscle contraction and preganglionic sympathetic/sacral parasympathetic outflow.

items.shortDefinition: Descending motor axon tract originating in M1/premotor Layer 5, descending through internal capsule and medullary pyramids (85-90% decussating).
items.biologicalRole: Conveys voluntary fine fractionated motor commands—especially skilled distal hand movements—to spinal interneurons and alpha motor neurons.

items.shortDefinition: Major ascending spinal white-matter pathways for pain/temperature (anterolateral) and fine touch/proprioception (gracile/cuneate DCML).
items.biologicalRole: Transmits somatotopically organized peripheral sensory information from the spinal cord and medulla to VPL thalamus.

items.shortDefinition: 31 pairs of segmental paravertebral ganglia housing pseudounipolar primary somatosensory and nociceptive neuron somata.
items.biologicalRole: Transduce mechanical, thermal, proprioceptive, and nociceptive stimuli from skin, muscle spindles, and viscera into central spikes.

items.shortDefinition: Bilateral paravertebral sympathetic chain and celiac/mesenteric ganglia innervated by thoracolumbar (T1–L2) preganglionic neurons.
items.biologicalRole: Releases norepinephrine (and adrenal epinephrine) onto cardiovascular, bronchial, and metabolic effectors during fight-or-flight mobilization.

items.canonicalName: Parasympathetic Terminal Ganglia & Enteric Nervous System
items.tnaLatinName: Pars parasympathica et Systema nervosum entericum
aliases: Parasympathetic Terminal Ganglia & Enteric Nervous System
Pars parasympathica et Systema nervosum entericum
items.shortDefinition: Craniosacral parasympathetic ganglia (ciliary, pterygopalatine, submandibular, otic, intramural) and myenteric/submucosal enteric plexuses.
items.biologicalRole: Mediates cholinergic rest-and-digest homeostasis, bradycardia, pupillary constriction, and autonomous gastrointestinal peristalsis.

items.canonicalName: Cranial Nerve I — Olfactory Nerve & Bulb
aliases: Cranial Nerve I — Olfactory Nerve & Bulb
items.shortDefinition: Special sensory nerve (SVA) formed by olfactory receptor axons traversing the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb glomeruli.
items.biologicalRole: Conveys odorant identity directly to olfactory bulb and piriform/amygdala/entorhinal cortex without a thalamic relay.

items.canonicalName: Cranial Nerve II — Optic Nerve, Chiasm & Tract
aliases: Cranial Nerve II — Optic Nerve, Chiasm & Tract
items.shortDefinition: CNS myelinated fiber tract formed by retinal ganglion cell axons hemidecussating at the optic chiasm en route to LGN, pretectum, and SCN.
items.biologicalRole: Transmits high-resolution retinotopic visual streams and non-image-forming circadian light intensity.

items.shortDefinition: Midbrain motor and parasympathetic nerve (GSE + GVE Edinger-Westphal) exiting the interpeduncular fossa through the superior orbital fissure.
items.biologicalRole: Innervates superior/inferior/medial recti, inferior oblique, levator palpebrae, and sphincter pupillae/ciliary muscles.

items.shortDefinition: Slender dorsal-exiting, fully decussating midbrain somatic motor nerve (GSE) at the level of the inferior colliculus.
items.biologicalRole: Innervates the contralateral superior oblique extraocular muscle to depress and intort the eye.

items.canonicalName: Cranial Nerve V — Trigeminal Nerve & Ganglion
aliases: Cranial Nerve V — Trigeminal Nerve & Ganglion
items.shortDefinition: Largest mixed cranial nerve (GSA ophthalmic V1, maxillary V2, mandibular V3 + SVE branchial motor) anchored in the pons.
items.biologicalRole: Conveys facial/corneal/dural touch, pain, and proprioception to VPM thalamus and innervates the muscles of mastication.

items.shortDefinition: Pontomedullary somatic motor nerve (GSE) whose nucleus coordinates conjugate horizontal gaze with contralateral CN III via the MLF.
items.biologicalRole: Innervates the ipsilateral lateral rectus muscle to abduct the eye.

items.shortDefinition: Mixed pontine nerve (SVE facial expression, SVA chorda tympani anterior 2/3 tongue taste, GVE lacrimal/submandibular parasympathetic).
items.biologicalRole: Drives mimetic facial expression, stapedius acoustic attenuation, anterior tongue gustation, and lacrimal/salivary secretion.

items.shortDefinition: Special sensory nerve (SSA) entering the cerebellopontine angle from the spiral (cochlear) and Scarpa's (vestibular) ganglia.
items.biologicalRole: Conveys auditory frequency/intensity from the organ of Corti and linear/angular head acceleration from the vestibular labyrinth.

items.shortDefinition: Mixed medullary nerve (SVA posterior 1/3 tongue taste, GVA carotid body/sinus baroreception, GVE parotid, SVE stylopharyngeus).
items.biologicalRole: Mediates carotid sinus baroreceptor reflex, posterior tongue taste, gag reflex afferent limb, and parotid salivation.

items.shortDefinition: Extensive mixed medullary nerve (GVE dorsal motor nucleus + nucleus ambiguus, GVA thoracoabdominal viscera, SVE pharyngeal/laryngeal).
items.biologicalRole: Principal parasympathetic outflow and interoceptive afferent highway linking heart, lungs, and gut to the NTS.

items.shortDefinition: Somatic/branchial motor nerve originating from upper cervical spinal segments (C1–C5) ascending through the foramen magnum.
items.biologicalRole: Innervates the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles for head rotation and shoulder elevation.

items.shortDefinition: Medullary somatic motor nerve (GSE) exiting between the pyramid and olive via the hypoglossal canal.
items.biologicalRole: Innervates intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles essential for speech articulation and swallowing.

items.canonicalName: Internal Capsule (Anterior Limb, Genu & Posterior Limb)
items.shortDefinition: V-shaped subcortical projection fiber bottleneck flanked by caudate/thalamus medially and lentiform nucleus laterally.
items.biologicalRole: Conveys thalamocortical radiations, corticospinal/corticobulbar motor tracts, and corticopontine fibers.

items.shortDefinition: Perisylvian association white-matter tract arching around the insula to link posterior temporal (Wernicke) and inferior frontal (Broca) cortices.
items.biologicalRole: Structural backbone of the dorsal phonological/articulatory language stream and frontoparietal attention network.

items.shortDefinition: Hook-shaped ventral association tract linking anterior temporal pole and amygdala with orbitofrontal/vmPFC cortex.
items.biologicalRole: Supports ventral semantic processing, episodic-valuation integration, and prefrontal regulation of amygdala reactivity.

items.shortDefinition: Medial limbic association tract running within the cingulate and parahippocampal gyri from subgenual ACC to entorhinal cortex.
items.biologicalRole: Connects medial prefrontal, posterior cingulate, and medial temporal hubs of the Papez circuit and Default Mode Network.

items.shortDefinition: C-shaped efferent/afferent fiber bundle arching from the hippocampal subiculum/CA1 to the mammillary bodies, septal nuclei, and anterior thalamus.
items.biologicalRole: Principal subcortical output highway of the hippocampal formation in the Papez episodic memory loop.

items.shortDefinition: Paired posterior hypothalamic nuclei receiving the postcommissural fornix and projecting via the mammillothalamic tract to anterior thalamus.
items.biologicalRole: Critical diencephalic relay for head-directiontheta signaling and recollective episodic memory.

items.shortDefinition: Dorsomedial diencephalic complex comprising the melatonin-secreting pineal gland and the habenular nuclei.
items.biologicalRole: Lateral habenula encodes negative reward prediction errors (disappointment/aversion) to inhibit VTA dopamine neurons; pineal secretes nocturnal melatonin.

items.canonicalName: Basal Forebrain Cholinergic Complex (Nucleus Basalis of Meynert)
items.shortDefinition: Substantia innominata cholinergic cell group providing widespread acetylcholine innervation across the entire neocortex and amygdala.
items.biologicalRole: Elevates cortical signal-to-noise ratio, desynchronizes slow waves during wake/REM, and gates sensory cortical plasticity.

items.shortDefinition: Oval rostral midbrain tegmental nucleus (magnocellular and parvocellular divisions) receiving dentate cerebellar and motor cortical inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Origin of the rubrospinal tract and dentato-rubro-olivary triangle supporting upper-limb motor coordination.

items.shortDefinition: Crumpled ventrolateral medullary nuclear lamina with Cx36 gap-junction-coupled oscillatory neurons giving rise to cerebellar climbing fibers.
items.biologicalRole: Delivers powerful complex-spike motor error teaching signals to contralateral cerebellar Purkinje dendrites.

items.canonicalName: Neural Retina (Photoreceptor, Bipolar, Amacrine & Ganglion Layers)
items.shortDefinition: Outpouching of embryonic diencephalon containing rods, cones, horizontal, ON/OFF bipolar, amacrine, and retinal ganglion cells.
items.biologicalRole: Transduces photons into graded potentials and center-surround ganglion spike trains transmitted via CN II.

items.shortDefinition: Fluid-filled snail-shaped inner ear sensory organ with basilar membrane tonotopy, electromotile outer hair cells, and inner hair cells.
items.biologicalRole: Mechanoelectrically transduces acoustic pressure waves into phase-locked spiral ganglion spike trains along CN VIII.

items.shortDefinition: Heavily myelinated extrastriate occipitotemporal area receiving direct magnocellular V1 Layer 4B and pulvinar inputs.
items.biologicalRole: Computes visual motion direction and speed, feeding parietal LIP/IPS accumulators during perceptual decision-making.

items.tnaLatinName: Campi oculares frontales et Sulcus intraparietalis
aliases: Campi oculares frontales et Sulcus intraparietalis
items.shortDefinition: Reciprocally coupled frontoparietal cortical nodes (BA 8 and IPS/LIP) projecting to superior colliculus and extrastriate visual cortex.
items.biologicalRole: Form the Dorsal Attention Network steering endogenous spatial attention and saccadic target selection.
